data.rationale: Scenario-owned durable data observed in the canonical data directory.

budget.rationale: Durable storage is bounded by the workload byte ceiling; it is alarm-only because the data is not regenerable.

storage.rationale: Storage surfaces are declared from observed canonical scenario directories; external resource databases are not claimed by this scenario.

service.name: scenario-authenticator
service.description: Multi-tenant identity provider (IdP) for the Vrooli fleet: realm-scoped accounts, RS256/JWKS token issuance with stateless local verification, sessions, MFA, federation, and API keys — consumed API-to-API by other scenarios and deployable as the auth backend for hosted products.

redis.purpose: Hot state: server-tracked sessions, token-family revocation, OAuth CSRF state, and distributed rate limiting. Optional at tier-1-local, where the durable local store behind the same Store seam keeps this state across restart. Required above one replica, because a revocation blacklist that is not shared does not revoke; that per-tier answer is recorded in tier_feasibility. Account persistence is SQLite via the api-core/storage seam (no shared Postgres).

tier-1-local.notes: The durable local store is the single-node default; Redis is an opt-in accelerator. The in-memory fake is a test double only, because dropping the revocation blacklist on restart re-admits a revoked token.

tier-2-desktop.reason: No vendorable cross-platform RESP server exists
tier-2-desktop.notes: Redis upstream publishes no native macOS or Windows build, Valkey ships source only, and Garnet's archives are framework-dependent rather than self-contained.

tier-4-saas.notes: Redis is required above one replica. The revocation blacklist and the rate-limit counters must be shared across replicas: a blacklist that is not shared does not revoke.

swappable_with.notes: A durable local store behind the same Store seam preserves the durability property across restart, but not cross-replica sharing. A deployment running more than one replica still needs a real Redis.
